state.case_summary: A 43-year-old man with no significant medical history presented in December with a 4-day history of fever to 38.8 °C, shaking chills, hemoptysis, and worsening dyspnea. He reported several months of intermittent night sweats, arthralgias of the wrists and ankles, and a 10-kg weight loss. One day before admission, he noted a painful ecchymotic lesion on his left calf; over the next 24 hours, similar lesions appeared on his abdomen, back, right upper arm, and right calf. His 3-year-old son had recently had a respiratory illness. On examination, temperature was 35.3 °C, blood pressure 117/75 mmHg, pulse 112 beats/min, respiratory rate 29 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Bilateral wheezes were present, and there were multiple painful ecchymoses with hemorrhagic bullae over the trunk and extremities. Laboratory studies showed a WBC count of 9000/mm3 (87% neutrophils), hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, normal renal and liver function, lactate dehydrogenase 799 IU/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate 81 mm/h, and C-reactive protein 38.5 mg/dL. Chest radiography and CT demonstrated multifocal alveolar infiltrates, and CT angiography showed no pulmonary embolism. Empiric intravenous ceftriaxone and oral azithromycin were started for presumed community-acquired pneumonia. On hospital day 2, a punch biopsy of a skin lesion revealed superficial and deep dermal thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy involving skin appendages without significant neutrophils or leukocytoclasia. Tests for cryoglobulin, protein C, protein S, rheumatoid factor, anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies, anti–double-stranded DNA antibodies, complement levels, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, and anti–glomerular basement membrane antibodies were negative. Antinuclear antibody titer was 1:160; lupus anticoagulant was prolonged at 82 seconds (reference range, 27–41); anticardiolipin IgM was 64 (reference range, 0–12); and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM was >100 (reference range, <10). Nasopharyngeal testing for influenza antigen, streptococcal antigen, and Legionella antigen was negative. A FilmArray respiratory panel was positive for respiratory syncytial virus and negative for other respiratory viruses and atypical bacteria. Epstein-Barr virus DNA PCR was positive at 8696 copies/mL; tests for HIV, cytomegalovirus, and hepatitis A, B, and C were negative.

root.label: Subacute Progressive Multisystem Syndrome with Constitutional Alarm Signs and Cutaneous Vasculopathy
excluded_candidates: Infectious pneumonia: negative nasopharyngeal testing for common pathogens, but positive for respiratory syncytial virus
Autoimmune vasculitis: negative tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies and anti–glomerular basement membrane antibodies, but positive for lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin IgM
Malignancy: no clear evidence, but significant weight loss and constitutional symptoms

B1.label: Infectious Disease
